mainTopic: Iron Mountain palms, minimum lengths of the ארבעה מינים, and the identity and עבות requirement of the הדס
overview: The amud opens with a second version of אביי's teaching about the לולב from צִינֵּי הַר הַבַּרְזֶל. A palm whose leaves reach one another is כשר, and one with bare gaps is פסול. An aggadic tradition places these palms at the entrance to גיהנם. The גמרא then sets the minimum lengths: שמואל says three טפחים for the הדס and ערבה and four for the לולב, and רבי יוחנן adds that the spine itself must rise one טפח above the הדס. רבי טרפון's 'אמה of five טפחים' is explained two ways, by רב דימי and by רבין. The rule that a rounded number is assumed only לחומרא shows that שמואל follows רבין's smaller measure. A new משנה lists what makes a הדס פסול, and the גמרא proves from the פסוק ״עֲנַף עֵץ עָבוֹת״ that the plant is the הדס, ruling out the olive tree, the דולבא and the הירדוף. It then defines עבות as three leaves per base, against רב כהנא's lenient two-and-one. The amud ends with אביי beginning to answer how a הדס that lost most of its leaves can still be עבות, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A contradiction about the Iron Mountain palms
steps.stepSummary: Some present אביי's teaching as a contradiction: the משנה says a לולב from צִינֵּי הַר הַבַּרְזֶל is כשר, but a ברייתא says it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some present it as a contradiction: We learned in the משנה that a לולב from the palms of the Iron Mountain is fit. But a ברייתא teaches that it is unfit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the earlier teaching. In this version it is a clash between two sources: the משנה says these palms are כשר and a ברייתא says they are פסול. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, אביי simply explained when the משנה's ruling applies. Here the same idea is framed as a contradiction between a משנה and a ברייתא. The underlying issue is the same: this palm's leaves are short and may not cover the whole spine.

keyTerms.meaning: And some present it as a contradiction (a second version of the teaching)
Palms of the Iron Mountain, a palm type with short, sparse leaves
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new argument. It is the same teaching of אביי told a second way, as a contradiction instead of a simple explanation.

phrases.english: And there are those who raise it as a contradiction:
phrases.notes: Introduces an alternate version of the previous teaching.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah: palms of the Iron Mountain are fit,
But isn't it taught in a baraita: it is unfit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second version of the earlier teaching of אביי on the previous section of the דף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that צִינֵּי הַר הַבַּרְזֶל are כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules the same palm פסול, so the two sources seem to directly contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי: it depends on whether the leaves overlap
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two sources deal with different cases. If each leaf's tip reaches the base of the next leaf, the לולב is כשר. If not, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no difficulty. Here (the משנה) is where the top of this leaf reaches the base of the next one. There (the ברייתא) is where the top of this leaf does not reach the base of the next one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. He shows that the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Iron Mountain palm has short leaves spaced apart on the spine. If each leaf reaches up to where the next one grows, the spine is fully covered and it looks like a normal לולב, so it is כשר. If there are bare gaps between the leaves, it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources address different cases
Here... there; splitting the two sources into two cases
Its top (the tip of a leaf)
Its base (where the next leaf grows from the spine)

steps.whatToRemember: A לולב from the Iron Mountain palms is כשר only if its leaves overlap enough to cover the spine.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
Here, where the top of this leaf
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה (fit).

phrases.english: reaches the base of that next leaf;
there, where the top of this leaf does not
phrases.notes: Refers to the baraita (unfit).

phrases.english: reach the base of that next leaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source addresses a different physical situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about the same palm.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is where the leaves reach each other (כשר); the ברייתא is where they leave gaps (פסול).

steps.title: Where the Iron Mountain palms are: the entrance of גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: A tradition, quoted in the name of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, says two palms stand in גיא בן הנם with smoke rising between them. These are the palms of the משנה, and that spot is the entrance to גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מריון said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, and some say רבה בר מרי taught it in the name of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: There are two date palms in the valley of בן הנם, and smoke rises from between them. This is what we learned: the palms of the Iron Mountain are fit. And that place is the entrance of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to identify where these palms grow. It quotes an aggadic tradition linking them to the entrance of גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step does not change the halacha. It explains which palms the משנה means. The tradition comes with two versions of its chain of transmission, given as "and some say."

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (an alternate chain of who said it)
The valley of בן הנם, outside ירושלים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מָרִיּוֹן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Maryon said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי
phrases.english: and some say Rabba bar Mari taught
in the name of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי תְמָרוֹת יֵשׁ בְּגֵיא בֶּן הִנֹּם,
phrases.english: There are two date palms in the valley of ben Hinnom,
and smoke rises from between them.
And this is what we learned:
Palms of the Iron Mountain are fit,
and that is the entrance of Gehenna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מָרִיּוֹן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side note identifying the location of the palms discussed in steps 1-2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Iron Mountain palms of the משנה are the two palms in גיא בן הנם, at the entrance of גיהנם.

steps.title: שמואל: minimum lengths of the four species
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's three-טפחים measure, שמואל rules: הדס and ערבה need three טפחים and the לולב needs four, so that the לולב rises one טפח above the הדס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "A לולב that has three טפחים." רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The measure of a הדס and a ערבה is three, and a לולב is four, so that the לולב sticks out one טפח beyond the הדס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its phrase about a three-טפחים לולב. שמואל then gives the exact minimum sizes for the species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל sets the הדס and ערבה at three טפחים and requires the לולב to be one טפח longer than the הדס, so its minimum is four. That extra טפח is what lets it be shaken above the bundle. This seems to clash with the משנה's 'three טפחים', which the גמרא takes up in step 6.
steps.whatToRemember: Minimums: הדס and ערבה are three טפחים; the לולב is four, so it extends one טפח above the הדס.
steps.whyThisMatters: These are the standard halachic minimum lengths used for the ארבעה מינים.

phrases.english: A lulav that has three handbreadths.
phrases.notes: Quotation of the משנה being explained.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The measure of a myrtle and a willow is three,
and a lulav is four,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא לוּלָב יוֹצֵא מִן הַהֲדַס טֶפַח.
phrases.english: so that the lulav extends a handbreadth beyond the myrtle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and returns to explaining the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הדס and ערבה need at least three טפחים; the לולב needs at least four, extending one טפח above the הדס.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the spine must stick out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that the extra טפח must be measured on the spine of the לולב itself, not on its leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי פרנך said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The spine of the לולב must extend one טפח beyond the הדס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a detail to שמואל's rule. He says exactly what part of the לולב must rise above the הדס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל alone, one might think the leaves sticking out past the spine could count toward the extra טפח. רבי יוחנן says the spine itself must extend one טפח beyond the הדס. The leaves on top do not count toward it.

keyTerms.meaning: The spine of the לולב (its central stem)

steps.whatToRemember: The one-טפח extension above the הדס is measured on the spine of the לולב, not the leaves.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Parnakh said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The spine of the lulav must
extend beyond the myrtle a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes שמואל's one-טפח rule more precise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spine itself, not just the leaves, must extend one טפח above the הדס.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: three טפחים seems enough for a לולב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, which seems to say a לולב of three טפחים is כשר. That clashes with שמואל, who requires four.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a לולב that has three טפחים, enough to shake it with, is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's rule that a לולב needs four טפחים. Our own משנה seems to say three is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the לולב must be four טפחים so it stands one טפח above the הדס. The משנה mentions only 'three טפחים' for the לולב. Read simply, the משנה contradicts שמואל.

phrases.english: We learned: a lulav that has in it
three handbreadths
enough to shake with it, is fit.
phrases.notes: On a simple reading, three טפחים alone is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לוּלָב שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the four-טפח לולב rule of שמואל (and of רבי יוחנן) from steps 4-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a לולב must be four טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names three טפחים as the length that makes a לולב כשר, which suggests four is not needed.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as three טפחים plus an extra טפח for shaking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה as 'three טפחים AND enough to shake it,' which means an extra טפח. שמואל and רבי יוחנן each measure that extra טפח their own way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: three טפחים, and in addition enough to shake it with, is כשר. Each Sage reads it according to his own view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה differently. The phrase 'enough to shake it' is not a description of the three טפחים. It is an extra amount on top of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a 'ו' ('and') turns 'enough to shake it' into an additional טפח, so the משנה also requires four. שמואל counts that extra טפח including the leaves. רבי יוחנן requires it on the spine of the לולב. So the משנה fits both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: This Sage according to his view

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the two Sages agree. Both accept that the extra טפח comes from the words 'enough to shake it.' They still argue about where that טפח is measured: with the leaves (שמואל) or on the spine (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.english: Say: and enough to shake with it, is fit.
phrases.notes: The added 'and' makes the shaking space an extra טפח.

phrases.english: This Sage according to his view,
phrases.notes: שמואל: the extra טפח may include the leaves.

phrases.english: and this Sage according to his view.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן: the extra טפח must be on the spine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 by reading the משנה's wording differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the source (adding 'and')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to make three טפחים alone enough for a לולב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means three טפחים plus an extra טפח for shaking, which agrees with both שמואל and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Attempted proof from a ברייתא that the four טפחים include the leaves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives three טפחים for הדס and ערבה and four for the לולב. The גמרא suggests the four includes the leaves, which would support שמואל over רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the measure of הדס and ערבה is three, and of the לולב four. Doesn't this mean including the leaves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to settle the argument between שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא simply says 'four' for the לולב without saying anything about leaves. The גמרא proposes that the plain meaning is the whole length, leaves included. That would back שמואל and argue against רבי יוחנן, who requires the extra טפח on the spine.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is about to be brought)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The measure of a myrtle and a willow is three,
and of a lulav, four.
Is it not including the leaves!
phrases.notes: That reading would support שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending both Sages to trying to decide between them.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the four טפחים of the לולב include the leaves
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving three טפחים for הדס and ערבה and four for the לולב

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: the four טפחים may exclude the leaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא could mean four טפחים not counting the leaves, which fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means apart from the leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא can be read the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא never mentions leaves, it can just as easily mean four טפחים measured without them. So it does not prove שמואל right. Both views remain standing.

phrases.english: No, apart from the leaves.
phrases.notes: This reading fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself, not שמואל's view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is ambiguous. 'Four' can mean four without the leaves.
steps.whatToRemember: Neither the משנה nor the ברייתא settles the argument. Both can be read to fit either שמואל (leaves count) or רבי יוחנן (spine only).

steps.title: The ברייתא in full: רבי טרפון's five-טפח אמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא itself, which also quotes רבי טרפון: the measures are given using an אמה of five טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא itself said: the measure of הדס and ערבה is three, and of the לולב four. רבי טרפון says: with an אמה of five טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the full ברייתא it just cited, to discuss the extra view of רבי טרפון it contains. This sets up רבא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה is normally six טפחים. רבי טרפון mentions an אמה of five טפחים. At first glance, רבא takes this to mean that the הדס must be five טפחים long instead of three.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (returning to analyze a quoted source)
A תנא who gives a different measure

phrases.english: The matter itself:
The measure of a myrtle and a willow is three,
and of a lulav, four.
Rabbi Tarfon says:
With a cubit of five handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 8 to study its full text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון ties the measurements to an אמה of five טפחים. At first this is understood as requiring a five-טפח הדס.

steps.title: רבא objects that רבי טרפון's measure is impossible in practice
steps.stepSummary: רבא says, 'May his Master forgive רבי טרפון.' People can barely find a dense-leaved הדס three טפחים long, so five would be almost impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: May his Master forgive רבי טרפון! We cannot even find a three-טפח עבות (dense-leaved) הדס. Do we even need to say a five-טפח one?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sharply attacks רבי טרפון's view. As רבא understands it, it demands a הדס length that people simply cannot find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is practical. A kosher הדס must be עבות, with thick leaves. Even three טפחים of that is rare, so five would be nearly unreachable. This challenge pushes us to ask whether רבי טרפון really meant five טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Dense-leaved, the required kind of הדס
Is it even necessary to say? (all the more so)

steps.confusionAlert: 'May his Master forgive him' is not an insult. It is a respectful way of saying a great Sage's ruling seems far too strict. Also, this objection rests on reading רבי טרפון as requiring five טפחים, which is only a first understanding of his view.

phrases.english: Rava said:
May his Master forgive Rabbi Tarfon.
Now, a dense-leaved one of three we do not find,
is one of five even a question!
phrases.notes: All the more so, a five-טפח one cannot be found.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁרָא לֵיהּ מָרֵיהּ לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבי טרפון's measure quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's view, understood as requiring a five-טפח הדס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dense-leaved הדס of even three טפחים is hard to find, so a five-טפח requirement would make the מצוה nearly impossible to keep.

steps.title: רב דימי: the cubit is divided into five larger handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that רבי טרפון takes a normal six-טפח אמה and divides it into five bigger טפחים. The הדס gets three of these, which equals three and three-fifths normal טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: take an אמה of six טפחים and make it into five. Take three of them for the הדס, and the rest for the לולב. How much is that? Three and three-fifths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's complaint. According to רב דימי, רבי טרפון never asked for a five-טפח הדס. He only made each טפח a bit bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא understood 'an אמה of five טפחים' to mean five full טפחים of length. רב דימי reads it as a way of measuring: split a regular six-טפח אמה into five equal parts, and use those larger parts as the טפחים. Three of them for the הדס comes to 3⅗ regular טפחים, which is much more realistic than five.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When he came', meaning a scholar who arrived in בבל from ארץ ישראל with a teaching
An אמורא who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל
Handbreadths, the basic unit of length

steps.confusionAlert: רבי טרפון is not changing the NUMBER of טפחים (still three for the הדס). He is changing the SIZE of each טפח.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.english: A cubit of six handbreadths
make it into one of five,
phrases.notes: Divide it into five larger handbreadths

phrases.english: take three of them for the myrtle,
and the rest for the lulav.
How much does that come to?
phrases.notes: In regular handbreadths

phrases.english: Three and three-fifths.
phrases.notes: Each large handbreadth is 6/5 of a regular one, and 3 × 6/5 = 3⅗

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection by reinterpreting רבי טרפון's 'אמה of five'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון requires a הדס five regular טפחים long
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון means larger טפחים, so the הדס is 3⅗ regular טפחים

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: With רב דימי's numbers, שמואל's two statements clash. He said the הדס needs three טפחים, but he also ruled like רבי טרפון, which comes out to 3⅗.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between שמואל and שמואל. Here רב יהודה said in שמואל's name that the measure of the הדס and ערבה is three, and there רב הונא said in שמואל's name that the halacha follows רבי טרפון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that, according to רב דימי, שמואל contradicts himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the halacha follows רבי טרפון as רב דימי explains him, the הדס must be 3⅗ regular טפחים. But שמואל elsewhere said plain 'three'. These two numbers do not match.

keyTerms.meaning: One statement of שמואל contradicts another statement of שמואל
'Here... and there', setting two sources side by side

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between Shmuel and Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Here Rav Yehuda said in Shmuel's name:
The measure of the myrtle and willow is three,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָם אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and there Rav Huna said in Shmuel's name:
The halacha follows Rabbi Tarfon!
phrases.notes: Which, by רב דימי's math, means 3⅗

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב דימי's explanation against שמואל's rulings
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's two statements, read through רב דימי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruling like רבי טרפון gives 3⅗ טפחים, but שמואל said three

steps.title: שמואל was only approximating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that when שמואל said 'three', he was speaking roughly and not precisely.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was not precise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a quick answer: שמואל's 'three' was a round number, not an exact measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real measure is 3⅗, and שמואל simply rounded it to three. This would remove the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He was not precise', meaning he spoke in round numbers

phrases.english: He was not precise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 13

steps.title: Rounding is acceptable only when it leads to stricter practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'not precise' answer. We say someone rounded only when the rounding makes things stricter, never when it makes things more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that we say 'he was not precise' in the direction of stringency, but do we say 'he was not precise' in the direction of leniency?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rounding 3⅗ down to three is a קולא, because people would use a הדס that is too short and therefore פסול. A sage may round in a way that asks for more than needed, but not in a way that lets people use something invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say that...', granting one point in order to challenge another

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general rule of 'לא דק': imprecision is allowed only לחומרא. That rule decides between רב דימי and רבין.

phrases.english: Granted we say 'he was not precise' toward stringency,
toward leniency do we say 'he was not precise'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמְרִינַן לָא דַּק לְחוּמְרָא, לְקוּלָּא מִי אָמְרִינַן לָא דַּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'not precise' answer as applied to רב דימי's numbers
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Rounding 3⅗ down to 3 would be a leniency, and approximation is never assumed לקולא

steps.title: רבין: the אמה is divided into six smaller טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבין explains that רבי טרפון takes a small five-טפח אמה and divides it into six smaller טפחים. The הדס gets three of these, which equals two and a half normal טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: take an אמה of five טפחים and make it six. Take three of them for the הדס, and the rest for the לולב. How much is that? Two and a half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different explanation of רבי טרפון. Here the טפחים become smaller instead of bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה of five regular טפחים is divided into six equal parts, and each part counts as a טפח. Three of them equal 2½ regular טפחים. This also answers רבא, since the הדס is now even shorter and easy to find.

keyTerms.meaning: Another אמורא who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: רבין reverses רב דימי's direction. רב דימי turns six into five (bigger טפחים), while רבין turns five into six (smaller טפחים).

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
A cubit of five handbreadths
make it into six.
phrases.notes: Divide it into six smaller handbreadths

phrases.english: Take three of them for the myrtle,
and the rest for the lulav.
How much does that come to?
Two and a half.
phrases.notes: Each small handbreadth is 5/6 of a regular one, and 3 × 5/6 = 2½

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing explanation to רב דימי's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון requires larger טפחים (רב דימי)
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון uses smaller טפחים, so the הדס is 2½ regular טפחים

steps.title: שמואל still seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: Even with רבין's numbers, שמואל's 'three' does not match the 2½ that follows from ruling like רבי טרפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, there is still a contradiction between שמואל and שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבין's explanation still leaves a gap between שמואל's two statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling like רבי טרפון now means 2½ טפחים, while שמואל said three. The numbers still differ, this time in the opposite direction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the end', meaning the problem still remains

phrases.english: In the end, there is a contradiction between Shmuel and Shmuel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the contradiction of step 13, now against רבין's numbers
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's two statements, read through רבין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruling like רבי טרפון gives 2½ טפחים, but שמואל said three

steps.title: Here שמואל rounded up, which is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל was not precise, and this time the rounding is לחומרא. So his ruling like רבי טרפון stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was not precise, and this is imprecision toward stringency, as רב הונא said in שמואל's name: the halacha follows רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction using רבין's explanation. שמואל's 'three' is a rounding up of 2½.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rounding 2½ up to three only makes people use a longer הדס than they need, which is a חומרא. Step 15 established that this kind of imprecision is acceptable. So שמואל truly holds like רבי טרפון as רבין explains him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is', identifying the case with a known category

steps.whatToRemember: Following רבין, the minimum הדס and ערבה is 2½ regular טפחים. שמואל said 'three' as a stricter round number. We assume 'לא דק' only when the rounding is לחומרא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the accepted measure is based on רבין's smaller טפחים. It also shows the rule that a rounded figure is assumed to be on the strict side.

phrases.english: He was not precise,
and this is imprecision toward stringency.
As Rav Huna said in Shmuel's name:
The halacha follows Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא דַּק, וְהַיְינוּ לְחוּמְרָא לָא דַּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 using the rule from step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Approximation in the direction of stringency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's 'three' contradicts the 2½ of רבי טרפון
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Three' is a stricter rounding of 2½, which is acceptable
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows רבי טרפון as explained by רבין: 2½ regular טפחים, rounded up to three by שמואל

steps.title: Things that make a myrtle unfit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the disqualifications of a הדס: stolen, dry, from an אשרה or an עיר הנדחת, a broken top, torn-off leaves, or more berries than leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A stolen or dry הדס is פסול. One that comes from an אשרה or from an עיר הנדחת is פסול. If its top was cut off, if its leaves were torn off, or if it has more berries than leaves, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the things that make a הדס unusable for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same kinds of פסולים the earlier משניות gave for the לולב: a מצוה done through a sin, something that is no longer fresh, and objects tied to עבודה זרה. One rule is special to the הדס: berries that outnumber the leaves. The next line of the משנה shows that this one can be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Myrtle branch, one of the ארבעה מינים
A tree that is worshipped as עבודה זרה
A city whose people were led into עבודה זרה. All its property must be destroyed.
Berries (here, the small berries of the myrtle)

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A stolen myrtle or a dry one is unfit.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: One from an idolatrous tree, or from a city led astray to idolatry, is unfit.
If its top was cut off, or its leaves were torn off,
phrases.notes: The גמרא later explains exactly what counts as 'torn off'.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ עֲנָבָיו מְרוּבּוֹת מֵעָלָיו — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: or its berries outnumbered its leaves, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the minimum measurements of the species (steps 4 to 18) and opens a new משנה about what disqualifies a הדס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הדס is פסול if it is stolen, dry, from an אשרה or an עיר הנדחת, has a broken top, has torn-off leaves, or has more berries than leaves.

steps.title: Fixing the berries, but not on the festival
steps.stepSummary: If the extra berries are picked off, the הדס becomes כשר. But you may not pick them off on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he reduced the number of berries, the הדס is כשר. But you may not reduce them on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a way to fix the last problem it listed, the extra berries. It also limits when that fix may be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Too many berries is not a permanent defect. Picking some off until they no longer outnumber the leaves makes the הדס כשר. Doing this on יום טוב is forbidden, because it would be like fixing an object to make it usable.

keyTerms.meaning: He reduced them (picked off some berries)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule 'not on יום טוב' does not mean the הדס stays פסול forever. It only forbids doing the fixing on יום טוב itself. If it was fixed before יום טוב, it is כשר.

phrases.english: But if he reduced them, it is fit,
and one may not reduce them on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fix for the berry disqualification from step 19, and a limit on when it may be done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Picking off the extra berries makes the הדס כשר, but this may not be done on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: The berry problem can be fixed. The others in the list cannot. Do the fixing before יום טוב.

steps.title: The verse's 'dense tree' is the myrtle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains ״עֲנַף עֵץ עָבוֹת״ as a tree whose leaves cover its wood, and says this is the הדס.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: ״עֲנַף עֵץ עָבוֹת״ means a tree whose leaves cover its wood. Which tree is that? You must say it is the הדס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing where in the תורה we learn that the 'dense tree' is the הדס. This sets up a series of challenges from other trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק never says 'myrtle'. It describes a tree, and the ברייתא turns that description into a test: the leaves must cover the wood. The ברייתא says only the הדס passes, and the next steps test that claim against other trees.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A branch of a dense tree' (ויקרא כג:מ)
'You must say', meaning there is no other choice

phrases.english: Gemara:
The Rabbis taught:
'A branch of a dense tree' —
a tree whose leaves cover its wood.
And which tree is that?
You must say it is the myrtle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by finding the source in the תורה for the הדס, the subject of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״עֵץ עָבוֹת″ means a tree whose leaves cover its wood, and that is the הדס.

steps.title: Maybe it means the olive tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the olive tree, whose leaves also cover its wood, does not fit the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is the olive tree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by suggesting another tree whose leaves also cover its wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only test is 'leaves cover the wood', the olive tree passes too. So the ברייתא's claim that 'it must be the הדס' looks too quick.

phrases.english: But say it is the olive tree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 21 that only the הדס fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'you must say it is the הדס'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The olive tree's leaves also cover its wood, so it fits the test just as well.

steps.title: The olive tree is not 'dense' in the right way
steps.stepSummary: The word עבות requires leaves arranged in a woven, chain-like pattern, and the olive tree does not have this.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need עבות, and the olive tree does not have it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word עבות adds a second test, and the olive tree fails it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבות means braided or chain-like: the leaves grow in a woven pattern. So the פסוק has two tests: leaves that cover the wood, and leaves that are woven. The olive tree passes the first test but fails the second.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is not there', meaning that tree does not have this feature

phrases.english: We require 'dense' (braided), and that is absent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the olive tree challenge from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a second requirement found in the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any tree whose leaves cover its wood would fit, including the olive tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leaves must also be woven (עבות), and the olive tree's leaves are not.

steps.title: Maybe it means the plane tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the דולבא, whose leaves do grow in a braided pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is the plane tree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again with a tree that does pass the עבות test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 made 'braided leaves' the deciding test. The דולבא has braided leaves, so it seems to fit the פסוק as well as the הדס.

phrases.english: But say it is the plane tree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 23, the גמרא tries another tree that passes that test.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only the הדס fits the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The דולבא has woven leaves, so it passes the עבות test.

steps.title: The plane tree's leaves do not cover its wood
steps.stepSummary: The דולבא fails the first test: its leaves do not cover its wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need leaves that cover the wood, and the plane tree does not have this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plane tree fails the other test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both tests are clear. The olive tree fails 'woven', and the דולבא fails 'covers the wood'. The הדס is the only one so far that passes both.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵינַן עֲנָפָיו חוֹפִין אֶת עֵצוֹ, וְלֵיכָּא.
phrases.english: We require its leaves to cover its wood, and that is absent.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵינַן עֲנָפָיו חוֹפִין אֶת עֵצוֹ, וְלֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the plane tree challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses the first requirement, which the ברייתא already stated
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Woven leaves alone would be enough, so the דולבא would fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both features are needed, and the דולבא lacks covering leaves.

steps.title: Maybe it means the oleander
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the הירדוף, which passes both tests.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is the oleander!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its strongest challenge: a tree that has both features.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הירדוף's leaves cover its wood and are also woven. The פסוק's description alone cannot rule it out, so a new kind of argument will be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Oleander, a poisonous plant with sharp leaves

phrases.english: But say it is the oleander!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two trees were ruled out, the גמרא brings one that meets both tests.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק must mean the הדס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הירדוף has both covering leaves and woven leaves, so the description fits it too.

steps.title: אביי: the תורה's ways are pleasant
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules out the הירדוף from ״דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי נוֹעַם״. The תורה would not command holding a poisonous, prickly plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It says about the תורה, 'Its ways are ways of pleasantness', and the oleander is not pleasant.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a general principle about the תורה rather than with the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הירדוף is poisonous and its sharp leaves stab the hand. A מצוה that hurts the person doing it does not fit the תורה's 'pleasant ways'. So the תורה could not have meant this plant.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Its ways are ways of pleasantness' (משלי ג:יז)

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle ״דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי נוֹעַם״ is used in other places in ש״ס to decide how the תורה should be read.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
'Its ways are ways of pleasantness,' and that is absent here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the oleander challenge from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a general principle about the תורה from another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הירדוף meets both tests, so it would fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה would not command using a harmful plant, so the הירדוף is excluded.

steps.title: רבא: love truth and peace
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a different פסוק, ״הָאֱמֶת וְהַשָּׁלוֹם אֱהָבוּ״. A plant that hurts goes against peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We learn it from here: 'Love truth and peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different source for ruling out the הירדוף. He agrees with the result but not with the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plant that stabs and poisons is the opposite of peace. אביי and רבא reach the same result, that the הירדוף is excluded and the 'dense tree' is the הדס. They differ only on which פסוק teaches it.
steps.whatToRemember: ״עֵץ עָבוֹת״ must have leaves that cover the wood and are woven. The olive tree fails 'woven', the דולבא fails 'covers', and the הירדוף is ruled out because it is harmful. Only the הדס is left.

phrases.english: Rava said: from here:
'Love truth and peace.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source from אביי's for the same answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different פסוק for the same principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think אביי's פסוק is the only source.
steps.terutzMaskana: Using a harmful plant goes against peace, so the הירדוף is excluded.

steps.title: The braided, chain-like plant is the myrtle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא ends the search: the plant whose leaves look braided and chain-like is the הדס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A plant braided like a braid, which looks like a chain, is the הדס.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the דולבא and the הירדוף, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that names the correct plant: the הדס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The search needed a plant whose leaves grow braided and also cover its wood. The הדס matches both, and it has none of the problems of the הירדוף. So the hunt for the identity of עץ עבות is settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Myrtle, one of the ארבעה מינים

steps.whatToRemember: The עץ עבות of the פסוק is the הדס. Its leaves grow in a braided, chain-like pattern.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Braided like a kind of braid
and looking like a chain,
that is the myrtle.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קָלוּעַ כְּמִין קְלִיעָה וְדוֹמֶה לְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת, זֶהוּ הֲדַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the הירדוף is rejected, the ברייתא gives the final identification.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עץ עבות is the הדס, recognized by its braided, chain-like leaves.

steps.title: A second sign: wood and fruit taste the same
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reaches the הדס in a different way. The עץ עבות is a tree whose wood and fruit taste alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: "A branch of a thick tree" means a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same. You must say this is the הדס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב gives another way to identify the הדס, based on taste rather than how the leaves look.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first sign was about looks: braided leaves. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds a sign based on taste: the wood and fruit taste the same. Both signs lead to the same plant, the הדס.

keyTerms.meaning: "A branch of a thick tree" (ויקרא כג:מ)
The taste of its wood and its fruit is the same
"You must say", meaning only one answer fits

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
"A branch of a thick tree"
means a tree whose wood and fruit have the same taste;
you must say this is the myrtle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, taste-based way of identifying the same plant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עץ עבות is the tree whose wood and fruit taste alike, which is the הדס.

steps.title: Only a thickly leaved myrtle is valid
steps.stepSummary: A תנא rules that a הדס that is עבות is כשר, and one that is not עבות is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Sage taught: A thick tree is valid, and one that is not thick is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the plant is the הדס, the גמרא adds a rule: the specific branch must itself be thickly leaved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the species is not enough. The word עבות is also a requirement for each branch, so a thin הדס is פסול even though it is a real הדס. This sets up the next question: what exactly counts as עבות?
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a non-עבות branch stops being a הדס. It is still a הדס by species. It simply cannot be used for the מצוה.

phrases.english: A Sage taught:
a thick tree is valid,
and one that is not thick is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from identifying the species to the quality required of each branch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הדס must be עבות to be כשר. A non-עבות הדס is פסול.

steps.title: What counts as thick?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact definition of עבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is considered "thick"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the coming opinions: how many leaves make a הדס count as עבות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in the last step depends on a clear definition. This question is not an attack. It asks for practical details.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is considered thick?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term used in the תנא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact leaf arrangement that makes a הדס count as עבות.

steps.title: רב יהודה: three leaves from each base
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה defines עבות as three leaves growing from each base on the stem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is when the leaves stand three by three at each base.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question: a הדס is עבות when every leaf base on the stem has three leaves coming out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three leaves at the same point on the stem form a ring that covers the wood. This creates the braided, chain-like look from the ברייתא. This is the strict definition.

keyTerms.meaning: Three by three, three at each spot
"Nest", the base on the stem where leaves grow out

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It is when three by three stand
leaves at each base.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: וְהוּא דְּקָיְימִי תְּלָתָא תְּלָתָא טַרְפֵי בְּקִינָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what counts as עבות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עבות means three leaves growing from each base.

steps.title: רב כהנא: even two plus one
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא is more lenient. Even two leaves from one base, with a third leaf from a different base, counts as עבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Even two and one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a second, more lenient definition of עבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב כהנא, the three leaves do not all need to grow from the same point. Two from one base plus one from a nearby base is enough. רב יהודה requires all three at one base.

keyTerms.meaning: Two and one: two leaves from one base, one from another

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Even two and one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תְּרֵי וְחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה and gives a more lenient answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two leaves from one base plus one from another also counts as עבות.

steps.title: רב אחא seeks out the two-and-one myrtle
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא would purposely look for a two-and-one הדס, out of regard for רב כהנא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רבא would seek out a two-and-one myrtle, since this ruling came out of רב כהנא's mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how one אמורא acted in practice. He went out of his way to use the kind of הדס that רב כהנא allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא did not just accept a two-and-one הדס. He actively preferred it, to show respect for רב כהנא's teaching. This practice supports רב כהנא's lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: Would seek out, make a special effort to find

phrases.english: Rav Acha the son of Rava
would seek out two and one,
since it came out of the mouth of Rav Kahana.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְהַדַּר אַתְּרֵי וְחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows practical support for רב כהנא's lenient definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, רב אחא בריה דרבא preferred a two-and-one הדס because רב כהנא had allowed it.

steps.title: מר בר אמימר: that is a הדס שוטה
steps.stepSummary: מר בר אמימר tells רב אשי that his father called the two-and-one הדס a "הדס שוטה", a wild myrtle.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר אמימר said to רב אשי: My father called that kind a wild myrtle (הדס שוטה).
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר אמימר pushes back against רב כהנא's lenient view. His father, אמימר, said the two-and-one kind is not a proper הדס at all for this purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it a הדס שוטה means it is a poor, wild kind of myrtle that does not have the true עבות quality. This undercuts רב כהנא's ruling and רב אחא's practice, and supports רב יהודה's demand for three at each base.

keyTerms.meaning: "Foolish" or wild myrtle, a lesser kind that is not proper עבות

steps.whatToRemember: There is a dispute over the definition of עבות. רב יהודה requires three leaves at each base. רב כהנא allows two plus one, but אמימר called the two-and-one kind a הדס שוטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The halacha follows the stricter view: a הדס needs three leaves at each base to count as עבות. That is why people look for a "משולש" הדס.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Ameimar said to Rav Ashi:
My father, that kind
he called a wild myrtle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אַבָּא לְהָהוּא הֲדַס שׁוֹטֶה קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the two-and-one הדס that רב כהנא allowed and רב אחא preferred.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב כהנא's lenient definition of עבות and רב אחא בריה דרבא's practice based on it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A two-and-one branch is a wild הדס without true עבות quality, according to אמימר.

steps.title: Most leaves fell off, but it is still thick
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if most of a הדס's leaves fell off it is still כשר, as long as it is still עבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If most of its leaves fell off and only a minority remained, it is valid, provided that its thickness remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a הדס that lost many leaves. It is still valid, but only if it still looks thick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of leaves lost is not what matters. What matters is whether the branch is still עבות. Even with only a minority of leaves left, the branch is כשר if the remaining leaves still keep the thick pattern.
steps.confusionAlert: Losing most of the leaves sounds like it would make the branch פסול, but it does not. The only test is whether the branch is still עבות.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If most of its leaves fell off
and a minority remained on it, it is valid,
provided that its thickness remains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the עבות requirement to a branch that lost leaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הדס that lost most of its leaves is כשר, as long as it is still עבות.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a הדס can lose most of its leaves and still be עבות, since עבות requires three leaves from each base.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling is difficult on its own terms. You said that if most of its leaves fell off, it is כשר. Then the ברייתא went on to teach: "as long as it is still עבות." But once two of every three leaves have fallen off, how could you ever find it still being עבות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the ברייתא from step 37. It argues that the two halves of the ruling cannot both be true at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on רב יהודה's definition in step 33, עבות means three leaves growing from each base. If most of the leaves fell off, the גמרא assumes that two out of every three are gone, which leaves only one per base. Then the condition of being עבות could never be met, so the ruling "most leaves fell, still כשר" seems impossible to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult. It signals that a source contradicts itself.
And then it goes on to teach
Its dense-leaved (עבות) quality is still intact
How can you find such a case?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a bare הדס is כשר. The question is that the ברייתא's case seems impossible: losing "most" leaves appears to rule out being עבות by definition.

phrases.english: This matter itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: Formula for an internal contradiction within one source.

phrases.english: You said: if most of its leaves fell off, it is fit,
and then it teaches:
provided that its dense-leaved quality remains intact.
Once two [of every three leaves] have fallen off,
phrases.notes: Assumes 'most' means two out of each set of three.

phrases.english: how can you find it still dense-leaved?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא quoted in step 37 for being self-contradictory.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא: 'נשרו רוב עליו כשר, ובלבד שתהא עבותו קיימת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עבות requires three leaves per base. If most leaves fell, which means two of every three, at most one leaf per base remains. So the condition of עבות can never be met, and the first ruling seems impossible.

steps.title: אביי begins: such a case can exist
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens his answer by saying that a case of a הדס losing most leaves yet remaining עבות can be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can find such a case.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to answer the contradiction by saying the case is possible. This line only sets up his answer. The explanation of how it works comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי rejects the assumption that the ברייתא describes an impossible case. He will go on to describe a specific situation where most leaves are gone but the עבות quality still remains.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the contradiction
You can find it (such a case exists)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can find it
phrases.notes: Echoes the question's wording 'היכי משכחת לה'. The details continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 38 by claiming the case is possible.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: identifying a scenario where both parts of the ברייתא hold (details follow).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing most leaves necessarily destroys the three-per-base pattern, so the ברייתא's case can never happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a real scenario where most leaves fell and the הדס is still עבות. אביי spells it out next.
